    10 September 2026

Geographic focus:
    Asia (Singapore, UAE/Fujairah), Middle East (Strait of Hormuz, Iran)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — recaps events since the Feb 2026 US/Israel attack on Iran
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — uncertainty around mini-supply shocks and volume constraints at current prices
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    Six months after the US/Israel attack on Iran triggered a Hormuz disruption, marine fuel supply squeezes at major hubs have largely normalised. Singapore bunkering is stable; Fujairah has recovered to ~40% of pre-war volumes. VLSFO prices are ~60% above pre-war levels — off March record highs but still elevated. Physical supply exists, but high prices are suppressing demand and creating uncertainty around blending stock availability. A key forward risk is price-driven volume constraint: replacement barrels exist but may not clear the market at current price levels.
